prefix:
# Rate limiting for the export API

## Context

Exports are generated synchronously and a single tenant can saturate the export workers. We will limit each tenant to a fixed number of concurrent export jobs.

## Limit

Each tenant may run at most 4 concurrent export jobs. Jobs beyond the limit are queued in arrival order rather than rejected.
section_request: Write the next section, on how queued jobs are reported to clients.
strong:
## Reporting queued jobs

A queued job returns 202 with a `position` field and a `Retry-After` header set from the median job duration. Clients poll the job URL; position drops as earlier jobs finish. If a tenant cancels a running job, the next queued job starts immediately and its position becomes 0.
weak:
## Reporting queued jobs

Keeping clients informed is an important part of any well-designed API, and queuing is no exception. A queued job returns 202 with a `position` field and a `Retry-After` header set from the median job duration. Clients poll the job URL; position drops as earlier jobs finish. In other words, a client can always see where its job stands in the queue, and that position goes down over time as the jobs ahead of it complete. If a tenant cancels a running job, the next queued job starts immediately and its position becomes 0. Overall, this approach gives clients a clear and predictable view of their exports.
held_constant: Same mechanism and details in the same order: 202 with position, median-based Retry-After, polling, cancellation. Neither variant repeats the prefix, so continuity is held.
notes: Weak adds an opening platitude, a sentence restating the one before it and a closing summary; it carries no information the strong variant lacks. Length differs by design (verbosity-bias probe).
